limitations.environment: Windows Node 24.21.0, standalone Vite/Nitro 3 synthetic consumer
limitations.reproduction: After generation, add server/api/content/[...].ts and run Vite build: native SOURCE_B0001 correctly rejects it. Remove that route and build again: Connections can time out acquiring connections-types-owners.json.lock. Observed in an isolated fresh consumer; the retry remains blocked in that affected consumer.
limitations.evidence: Operational model-vite-canonical-fresh.log; no real data or application files involved.
limitations.handling: Unresolved upstream build-tool issue, outside runtime Model authorization/publication. No workaround or patch is introduced. Normal valid-config acceptance runs in independent clean consumers; recovery after an invalid configuration is not claimed. Native errors remain failures. Liti never deletes native lock/ownership bookkeeping or applies database migrations to recover a build.
limitations.removalCondition: An upstream-fixed distribution must reject the conflicting route and then successfully build after its removal, preserving native ownership locking.

fixes.symptom: On Windows with an 8.3 TEMP path (including GitHub's RUNNER~1 profile), native Vite types prepare treats the same generated Content route as a conflicting handler (SOURCE_B0002). The equivalent canonical physical TEMP path succeeds.
fixes.environment: Windows Node 24.21.0 and the pinned full-commit distribution; standalone Vite/Nitro 3 consumer, without Nuxt.
fixes.reproduction: The actual preview Windows consumer failed in run 40501231673. A local installed-distribution reproduction with TEMP/TMP set to a valid 8.3 alias fails types prepare; its canonical-path control succeeds.
fixes.scope: Canonicalize the existing CLI project directory and consumer temporary root using Node's public realpath API before invoking the native toolchain. Standalone Vite consumers must also start from a canonical physical project path; direct native execution from 8.3 aliases remains unsupported. No process-wide chdir, Model alias/dedupe layer, Source patch, storage change or route-guard bypass is introduced.
fixes.verification: The unmodified preview reproduces SOURCE_B0002 with a short TEMP path, while its canonical-path control and full canonical Vite production/dev/HMR runner pass. The complete consumer runner with a short TEMP environment and canonicalized invocation is being verified.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove the CLI/consumer realpath normalization and pass native types prepare, generation, build, HTTP and HMR in a fresh Windows consumer invoked through a valid 8.3 TEMP path. Native Content owner identity, Workspace validation and real user-owned route collision rejection must remain intact. Retain the regression tests.

fixes.symptom: The Liti-free Console/Agent-enabled Nuxt dev server reaches the default Node V8 heap limit near 4 GiB while generating server sourcemaps. Tree-shaking alone does not resolve it. Production Node/workerd builds are unaffected.
fixes.environment: Windows Node 24.22.1 and the pinned full-commit native distribution; normal Node heap settings.
fixes.reproduction: Run the Liti-free fixture's node verify-node.mjs --dev without dev-runtime. Both the unchanged configuration and tree-shaking-only attempt fail with Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit.
fixes.scope: Only in Nuxt dev, disable Nitro server sourcemap generation through public NitroConfig.sourceMap. Client maps, typechecking, runtime validation, error handling, storage and production builds are unchanged. Dev server stack traces lose server sourcemap mapping until this can be removed.
fixes.verification: The native-only server starts in about 21 seconds with the default heap and passes native Auth/Console/Content/Database/Agent/Schedule HTTP contracts. Packed Liti also passes model-definition HMR, authenticated writes and private SSR after reloading.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove the sourceMap assignment and run native-only plus packed Liti dev/HMR probes on Windows and Linux with default server sourcemaps and normal Node heap settings. Startup, authenticated writes, SSR and HMR must pass without exceeding the heap limit. Keep the generated-module inline fix until its independent regression also passes.

fixes.symptom: Nuxt dev externalizes the generated .nuxt/vitehub/database/local-runtime.mjs. Node then imports the application's untransformed TypeScript Database Definition and fails resolving its extensionless auth-schema import; the homepage and Auth return 500.
fixes.reproduction: After resolving the sourcemap memory failure, start the native-only dev consumer without the generated-module inline matcher. Observe Cannot find module server/database/auth-schema imported from server/databases/config.ts.
fixes.scope: A public Nitro externals.inline matcher only includes ViteHub's generated directory under Nuxt's actual buildDir, with normalized Windows separators. It retains the selected native Database, schema and driver. Liti's own generated directory is independently registered for normal bundling by liti/nuxt.
fixes.verification: With the matcher, the native-only dev consumer passes durable Auth signup/session, native SQL constraints and the remaining HTTP contracts. No .ts extension changes or runtime loaders were added to application definitions.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove the inline matcher and pass the native-only and packed Nuxt dev probes using unmodified ordinary application imports. Auth and SQL must execute the transformed native generated module without raw-Node module-resolution failures. Remove the file and registration when its separate sourcemap assignment is also obsolete.

fixes.symptom: The provided Nuxt bridge emits a Schedule dev handler importing #vitehub/schedule/registry but does not forward Schedule's existing Vite resolver/load hooks to Nitro 2. Dev output retains an unresolved bare import.
fixes.reproduction: Without the Schedule resolver hunk, native-only Nuxt dev logs Could not resolve import #vitehub/schedule/registry and leaves the unresolved import in .nuxt/dev/index.mjs.
fixes.scope: Add the installed Schedule Vite plugin to the existing resolver/replay allowlist. The native registry renderer, Schedule authorization and runtime are reused unchanged. This does not claim support for the separately documented Nuxt Schedule CLI dev transport.
fixes.verification: Native-only dev compiles the existing registry without unresolved-import warnings and passes the native scheduled-snapshot/duplicate-execution contracts.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove this hunk from both patch copies, install an upstream-fixed Nuxt bridge, and pass the same dev generated-output assertion and native Schedule runtime contracts. Remove the shared patch entry only after its independent Env and Console-error hunks are also obsolete.

fixes.symptom: The public consoleActionError helper does not mark its H3 error for the owning action adapter. A valid Console editor save reaches Model validation, but an invalid field is returned as a generic 500 with its issues discarded.
fixes.reproduction: In the packed Liti consumer, save a valid Console post, then save an empty required title with its reviewed digest. Without this hunk the response is 500; the expected response is 400 with validation details.
fixes.scope: One line marks the public helper's error with the existing private actionFailureKey. Native readActionFailure still restricts exposed failures to 4xx; authorization and error handling remain active.
fixes.verification: The installed distributed Console RPC returns 400 on invalid fields and still saves/publishes valid input on Node and workerd.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove this hunk from both patch copies, reinstall a fixed installed distribution and pass the same native Console RPC validation/save/publication tests on Node and workerd. Remove the patch entry only when its Env transform hunk is also obsolete.

fixes.symptom: The pinned public API cannot unpublish a document while retaining its newer draft, or atomically commit Model publication integrity metadata with the native Content publish scope. Raw Workspace deletion from published is correctly rejected with CONTENT_R0013. This is an explicitly tracked API feature gap, not a native bug or replacement CMS implementation.
fixes.environment: Installed full-commit distribution; Node 24.22.1 and workerd with native D1/R2.
fixes.reproduction: Model unpublish using the public Workspace history.commit({ ref: 'published', changes: { delete: [documentPath] } }) rejects with CONTENT_R0013. Deleting the draft first is not acceptable because it loses later edits.
fixes.scope: Expose commitPublished on the installed Content runtime and its declarations. It uses the existing native publication scope, conditional Workspace commit, validators and publish listeners. Direct Workspace deletion guards remain unchanged. Confirm an exact transaction receipt after a write:after failure and return explicit postCommitErrors; still notify native listeners after a committed transaction.
fixes.verification: Packed independent consumer rejects unauthorized direct Content, Console, raw Workspace deletion and commitPublished calls; Model unpublish preserves the draft, atomically checks incoming references and keeps the original publication date. A failing post-commit hook returns a committed receipt with sanitized warnings on Node and workerd.
fixes.removalCondition: Adopt an installed upstream public publication transaction with equivalent validators, CAS, draft-preserving deletion, atomic metadata and post-commit notification semantics. Replace the single Model integration call, remove both patch copies and root/consumer patch entries together, then pass the same packed Node/workerd contracts without the patch. Keep every regression. Until then, consumer roots must explicitly apply this identical patch; npm/pnpm without an equivalent configured patch are unsupported for Content writes.

fixes.symptom: Nuxt build succeeds with unresolved generated handlers, but the built Node server exits with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Workspace plugin is registered relative to server/; Windows handler paths contain backslashes that are interpreted as JavaScript escapes.
fixes.environment: Windows; Node 24.22.1; Bun 1.4.4; Nuxt 4.6.2 / Nitro 2.13.5; Vite 8.3.5; selected full-commit preview
fixes.reproduction: Remove generatedPaths from fixture modules, run bun run build, then node .output/server/index.mjs. Observed unmodified failure before adding the workaround. A consumer with prerender routes also reproduced an escaped .vitehub/nitro/database/request-stats.mjs handler in the separate prerender Nitro instance, failing with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME even while the main instance was normalized.
fixes.prerenderScope: Normalize the real Nitro build:before and prerender:init options through public hooks. Prerender replays native Database modules into its own instance; no private _config edits or disabled prerendering are used. Both native-only and packed fixtures retain a prerender route as a regression.
fixes.standaloneEnvironment: Vite 8.3.5 / Nitro 3.0.260903-beta without Nuxt on Windows. The same distributed Content handler path contains raw Windows backslashes and fails in #nitro/virtual/routing.
fixes.standaloneVerification: Unmodified distribution fails resolving C:Users...content<carriage-return>oute.mjs. A public Nitro module captures the host and public Vite build/dev hooks normalize options and resync native routing after async config completion. The packed Nuxt-free consumer builds and verifies native SQL uniqueness/FKs and Content authorization/save/publish/history in production and dev, including server-route HMR. Model's normal server-environment noExternal registration keeps native virtual Database configuration visible inside packaged server modules. Strict checking reports 151 existing native diagnostics and no added Model diagnostics; source/SDK errors fail the check.
fixes.removalCondition: On Windows and Linux, remove fixture and production registrations/files and verify clean install, prepare, build and the packed Node/Worker probes without unresolved generated imports. Retain the runtime regression. No application patch has been applied.

fixes.symptom: Workspace require shim evaluates in a non-entry chunk before Node entry initialization. Nitro supplies file:///_entry.js, which createRequire rejects on Windows.
fixes.reproduction: After normalizing generated paths, build the unpatched Node fixture and run verify-node.mjs: ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE for file:///_entry.js.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove both root/consumer patchedDependencies and both patch copies, reinstall, then build and run the Node probe on Windows/Linux. Non-entry import.meta must initialize with a valid actual module URL. Keep the runtime probe.

fixes.symptom: Enabling Console traces libSQL JS and package metadata but omits win32-x64-msvc/index.node; the production server exits with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
fixes.reproduction: Enable fixture Console without libsqlNative, build, then run verify-node.mjs.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove the registration/file and verify the installed Windows x64 native binding is included automatically and the built Console consumer starts. Other platforms are not covered by this workaround.

fixes.symptom: Nuxt Cloudflare Console build tries to resolve unused optional advocaat / Discord / Teams peers. The first failure is Cannot resolve advocaat and externals are not allowed.
fixes.reproduction: bun run test:vitehub:cloudflare without this patch fails resolving advocaat.
fixes.verification: The built Console Worker boots under workerd without these unused optional peers; Auth, Content, Database constraints and offline mock Agents execute.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove consumer patchedDependencies and both patch copies, reinstall the selected fixed distribution, then pass Cloudflare build and workerd Auth/Content/Console/mock-Agent tests with those optional peers absent. Retain the regression. App patch propagation is pending the package gate.

fixes.symptom: cachedSource imports nitro/cache (Nitro 3), pulling its H3 2 runtime through Nuxt Nitro 2/H3 1 aliases and failing at h3/rules.
fixes.reproduction: Remove nitroCache registration and build the Cloudflare fixture: h3/dist/index.mjs/rules cannot resolve.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove registration/file and pass Node/Worker builds plus the real cachedSource key-isolation/runtime check. The alias targets the host's native Nitro cache implementation, never an empty module.

fixes.symptom: The Nuxt bridge forwards resolver hooks but omits the Env Vite transform. Wrangler then cannot resolve the computed #vitehub/env/server import in built server code.
fixes.reproduction: With the cache workaround but without this patch, build the Cloudflare fixture and start verify-cloudflare.mjs: unresolved #vitehub/env/server.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove the consumer entry and both copies, reinstall the fixed distribution and boot the built Node/Console Worker without unresolved Env imports. The patch forwards only the installed Env plugin transform.

fixes.symptom: Nitro adds no_nodejs_compat_v2 even for modern compatibility dates, disabling the native Node modules required by the compiled ViteHub Console. Wrangler fails at fs/child_process in detect-libc.
fixes.reproduction: Without this patch hunk, boot the generated Cloudflare fixture: bare fs/child_process fail. Explicit nodejs_compat_v2 also conflicts with ViteHub's nodejs_compat flag.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove this hunk from both copies and pass the modern-date generated-config assertions and workerd probe without overriding the generated flags. Legacy dates retain the old default.

fixes.symptom: The generated Schedule plugin imports definePlugin from Nitro 3 even in Nuxt's Nitro 2 host. Build fails because H3 1 has no toRequest export.
fixes.reproduction: Enable schedule: true and remove schedulePlugin from Nuxt modules; the Cloudflare build fails at nitro/dist/runtime/nitro.mjs importing toRequest.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove registration/file and pass builds and the discovered Worker scheduled handler with native Nitro 2. Only the generated Schedule plugin import is transformed; native defineNitroPlugin and the original handler remain intact.

fixes.symptom: Enabling the native Blob serve route in Nuxt generates .vitehub/blob/serve-route.ts which fails TS2345: IncomingMessage has no arbitrary symbol index signature. The runtime only reads known request fields; a structural symbol index is not part of the Node HTTP contract.
fixes.reproduction: Set blob.serve.route to /media and run nuxt typecheck on an otherwise valid generated application. The unpatched application fails at blob.store(storeName).serve(event, pathname, options).
fixes.regression: test/fixtures/integration enables the native generated Blob route; packed Nuxt typecheck plus Node/workerd Blob GET/HEAD byte/content-type assertions in __blog.post.ts.
fixes.removalCondition: Remove this patch and the root entry with an upstream-fixed distribution; the native generated route must typecheck and pass the same GET/HEAD tests on Node and workerd without relaxing TypeScript checks.

featureGaps.evidence: The installed Nuxt bridge imports the built-in Content owner factory by a module specifier; there is no public callback to replace only its write operations with Model-authorized operations. Native Content calls do not authorize themselves.
featureGaps.decision: Use Nuxt's public Nitro alias hook to register one small owner factory which delegates to the public @vite-hub/content/runtime/console factory for native editing and wraps management writes in Model authorization, validation and reviewed digests. Direct native writes remain denied by Workspace validation. Translation writes requiring sparse semantics use the supplemental model controls.
featureGaps.removalCondition: When an installed public owner/write registration hook exists, replace the single alias registration and retain authenticated native Console, direct-write denial, field validation and publication tests. This bridge adds no Console component copies.

featureGaps.evidence: Installed Content DocumentsOptions offers schema fields and Markdown components. ConsoleSchemaFieldKind and ConsoleDocumentActionName enumerate fixed field/action sets; contributed sections/pages also use fixed built-in views. No arbitrary relation-picker, translation-operation or proofreading-button slot is exposed by these contracts.
featureGaps.decision: Prefer native Console for models whose invariants it can enforce. Implement only missing model controls in Liti Nuxt admin pages behind the same server authorization/validation boundary; do not copy Console internals or patch new features into upstream.

featureGaps.evidence: Native Content schedule calls publish({ expect }) and intentionally fails after draft edits. This is not a bug.
featureGaps.decision: Use a native Schedule Definition to publish an immutable Workspace revision. Store queue metadata in a Workspace ref and commit a receipt with published content in one native history CAS commit; later drafts are untouched. Revalidate authorization/model rules at execution. Do not rely on the scheduler's default run store for exactly-once publication.
featureGaps.owner: Model publication integrity + ViteHub Schedule; production implementation in phase 3
